raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Battery Park behind, head for the New York Stock Exchange, about a sixteen-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Walk around Castle Clinton, past the ferry terminal, and head inland toward the tall buildings.","source_id":"16827731-e514-47aa-a5e1-384aaf070f66","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Look for the scraggly little buttonwood tree out front — a sycamore, easy to miss.","source_id":"3aefff42-6156-46cc-8cea-e9e23a69cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["32c83e75-9249-4709-9232-95b42192c751"]},{"text":"It stands in for the buttonwood where twenty-four brokers gathered in 1792 to trade the young nation's Revolutionary War debt — the first stock market in America.","source_id":"3aefff42-6156-46cc-8cea-e9e23a69cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["eb5fe636-f060-41ad-adc8-4996b9f2ed1f","32c83e75-9249-4709-9232-95b42192c751"]},{"text":"Raise your eyes from that twig to the columns above, and you're looking at the world's most famous — some say infamous — financial institution.","source_id":"eb5fe636-f060-41ad-adc8-4996b9f2ed1f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The towering columns, the crowded pediment, the huge flag all trumpet might and prestige, far grander than the plain Federal Hall across the street.","source_id":"eb5fe636-f060-41ad-adc8-4996b9f2ed1f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And here's the odd part — though the world links it forever with Wall Street, its front actually faces Broad Street.","source_id":"3aefff42-6156-46cc-8cea-e9e23a69cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The real buttonwood stood further east, on Wall Street itself, and the deal the brokers struck there became known as the Buttonwood Agreement.","source_id":"32c83e75-9249-4709-9232-95b42192c751","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"As the history called Gotham puts it, that agreement \"laid the foundations for a structured securities market.\"","source_id":"32c83e75-9249-4709-9232-95b42192c751","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Early the next year the traders moved indoors, to the Tontine Coffee House at the corner of Water and Wall.","source_id":"32c83e75-9249-4709-9232-95b42192c751","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That corner hides an ugly past — it had been the site of the Royal African Trading Company, where the English bought and sold enslaved Africans.","source_id":"32c83e75-9249-4709-9232-95b42192c751","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Across the way, on the southeast corner of Broad and Wall, look for a building with no sign at all.","source_id":"0eeed6bb-fbde-4fca-bc89-657134782d48","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That's J. P. Morgan's bank.","source_id":"0eeed6bb-fbde-4fca-bc89-657134782d48","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Morgan wanted it plain — if you didn't know what it was, you had no business being there.","source_id":"0eeed6bb-fbde-4fca-bc89-657134782d48","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Its only decoration is a scatter of pockmarks along the Wall Street side, scars from a bomb blamed on anarchists that killed thirty-eight people and wounded hundreds in 1920.","source_id":"0eeed6bb-fbde-4fca-bc89-657134782d48","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Morgan left them there as a testament to his own invincibility.","source_id":"0eeed6bb-fbde-4fca-bc89-657134782d48","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The exchange gives no public tours now, but you can raise a coffee to the brokers over in Zuccotti Park, birthplace of Occupy Wall Street.","source_id":"3aefff42-6156-46cc-8cea-e9e23a69cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That's the New York Stock Exchange — a scraggly tree out front, and a bank next door that kept its scars.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1}]}
